tasks.task: Plan the campaign from pre-launch to the final day

items.when: When a creator decides to crowdfund and has, or can get, written quotes
When the plan needs one brief with goal, audience, messages and a weekly calendar
When dates depend on samples, making and freight, to date every step with an owner
When the plan looks finished, to imagine it failed and find the hidden assumptions

tasks.task: Choose the platform and check the reward model

items.when: Before any page work, when the creator is choosing between Kickstarter and Indiegogo
When the creator wants to offer profit share, equity or calls backers investors

tasks.task: Test demand before committing to a campaign

items.when: When nobody has proved people want it, to find what could kill it and run one cheap test
When you need what people already post about the problem, with links
When a sign-up page or deposit test should have a clear pass mark before launch
When the creator is sure of the idea and needs it tested against evidence
When survey answers say people would back it, to test how far to trust them

tasks.task: Set the funding goal from real costs

items.when: When you have quotes and need a goal where raising exactly 100% still delivers
When the making cost is one lump, to split it by part and maker
When you have a quote and freight, to get the cost per sellable unit and margin
When a factory quote arrives, for a quick cost per unit and a go or no-go
When the goal was picked to look reachable, to check the full costs behind it

tasks.task: Get and compare maker quotes for the first run

items.when: When no written quote exists, to ask makers in their own terms
When quotes use different units, currencies or delivery terms, to line them up
When the run size is set, to plan what to ask for and what to give back
When you must decide how many extra units to make beyond the pledges

tasks.task: Design and price reward tiers and add-ons

items.when: When you need five to eight tiers, each checked for profit after fees and shipping
Before pricing, to ask the pre-launch list what they would really pay
When you want to compare tier layouts and how the savings are worded
When you must decide the price digits and how add-ons are priced and shown
When a tier is priced, to check the true margin with every cost counted

tasks.task: Work out shipping, duties and tax for each destination

items.when: When you know parcel sizes and countries, to set zones and rates to charge
When rewards cross borders, to find tariff codes, duty options and customs papers
When freight quotes arrive, to compare them with every charge counted
When shipping costs change, to re-check that each tier still makes money

tasks.task: Plan stretch goals and add-ons that still make money

items.when: Before promising a stretch goal, to see what it adds to cost at each funding level
When an add-on or upgraded tier needs its price and margin checked
When a stretch goal upgrades every unit, to see the margin left after it

tasks.task: Write the campaign page

items.when: When you need the page written in the order backers read it
When the product sounds like others on the platform, to find one idea to lead with
When the title and first line are flat, to get five options with a subhead
When the risks section says only that the team has experience
When the page is drafted, to rank what would stop a visitor pledging
Before launch, to check each claim about the product against what you can show
When the page lists features and should tell a story and admit the drawback

tasks.task: Script the campaign video

items.when: When you need the video script timed to match the page
When the creator will speak to camera, to get a script with several openings
When the script is agreed and the shoot needs timed shots and an edit list
Before filming, to tighten the script and check it works with the sound off

tasks.task: Brief the photos, GIFs and page graphics

items.when: When a photographer needs a shot list with the reason for each shot
When the page needs a short GIF or clip that shows the product working
When the page needs a header or tier graphic, to get a prompt and exact size

tasks.task: Build the pre-launch list

items.when: Six to ten weeks out, to plan list growth with weekly sign-up targets
When you need the teaser, the preview and the sign-up page planned in order
When the sign-up page itself needs writing for one action
When sign-ups should bring friends, to set the reward and the flow
When the sign-up page is live and too few visitors join the list

tasks.task: Run small ads to grow the list and test the message

items.when: When you need several hooks and formats to test before launch day
When the ads need Facebook and Instagram text and hooks ready to run
When you set up the test: how to name each ad, cap spend and decide
Before spending, to know the most you can pay for a backer and still deliver

tasks.task: Write pre-launch and launch-day emails

items.when: When you need the emails to the creator's own list from teaser to launch day
When the campaign has a fixed close date and the whole run of emails needs planning
When each email needs subject lines in several angles to choose from
When an email is drafted, to get cuts, a pacing check and a ship or fix verdict

tasks.task: Pitch press, reviewers and creators

items.when: When the launch is news, to get a media list, pitch emails and a press kit outline
When the budget is small, to plan press before ads and the one idea to own
When reviewers or creators should get a prototype, to find, brief and track them

tasks.task: Write campaign updates and answer backers

items.when: When you need the schedule and words for updates from launch to delivery
When each update also needs posts made for each social platform
When comments and messages pile up and each needs a reply in the right tone
When backers gather in a group or forum and need a plan to keep them involved

tasks.task: Rescue a campaign that has stalled mid-run

items.when: When pledges have flattened and the creator wants a plan for the days left
When another creator or brand could share the campaign with their audience
When the middle weeks need a new reason to pledge that is not a price cut

tasks.task: Plan the final 48 hours

items.when: Three to four days before the deadline, to plan the last emails, updates and posts
When writing last-chance lines, to keep every limit and deadline true
When the reminder email needs several subject lines to pick from

tasks.task: Run the pledge manager and fulfilment after funding

items.when: When the campaign ends funded and the work moves to surveys, making and shipping
When factory samples arrive, to get go or hold and the fixes to send back
Before the final payment, to brief an inspector and set a pass rule
When a warehouse will pack and ship rewards, to request prices and set terms
When stock is on the water, to track it and warn the warehouse

tasks.task: Tell backers about a delay or problem

items.when: When a date slips, to state the loss, the numbers and the next step plainly
When the mistake was yours, to own it and state the fix in a short email
When rewards are shipping, to plan tracking updates and a delay script
When a backer asks for a refund, to reply with a clear yes, partial or no
When the update is drafted, to check it fits the update schedule and tone so far

tasks.task: Move to late pledges and a pre-order store

items.when: When the campaign has closed and late backers still want to order
Before the pre-order store opens, to check it is ready to take orders
When late buyers need thank-you, add-on and delivery emails

tasks.task: Review a finished campaign

items.when: When you have pledge sources, to see which channels brought backers and at what cost
When the campaign is over, for a one-page note on what to repeat and change

always.when: When a page or update states a number, date or award you cannot trace to the creator
Before anything is published, to fix lines that sound machine-written
Before a page or update goes live, to catch typos and tier names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the campaign video needs shooting and editing, not only a script
When the page needs product photos and GIFs made, not only briefed
When ads run at real spend and need daily budget and creative decisions
When press outreach is a main channel and needs a media list worked daily
When the product is not yet ready to quote: samples, tooling, safety tests
When rewards ship to many countries and need freight, customs and a warehouse

gaps: No library item is about crowdfunding at all; every library item here is borrowed from launches, stores or supply
No library item sets a funding goal from costs, fees and a failure margin; only the kit skill does
No library item prices reward tiers with platform fees, early-bird limits and shipping by destination
No library item plans stretch goals or add-ons and tests what each does to cost per backer
No library item writes a Kickstarter or Indiegogo page, or checks one against the platform's rules
No library item writes backer updates or plans their schedule; only the kit skill does
No library item covers pledge managers, backer surveys, address collection or tax and VAT on rewards
No library item offers different campaign page or video concepts to compare, or checks page images and GIFs
No library item reads live campaign numbers day by day to say whether the campaign is on track to fund
No library item finds and pitches crowdfunding press, newsletters or cross-promotion with other campaigns
